buyer: Commodity and industrial PMs, policy teams
pain: Critical mineral supply is a strategic risk nobody maps well
v1: A supply map for one mineral with China processing detail
verdict: Strong theme and real access advantage, though specialist commodity houses already compete.

why.distribution: Warm fund contacts, though commodity specialists are a narrower slice of her network.
why.demand: Commodity research is a well-established paid category.
why.fmf: Generalist analysis plus China processing access; she lacks mining sector depth.
why.defensibility: China processing visibility is genuinely scarce.
why.tailwind: Critical minerals sit at the centre of both energy transition and industrial policy.
why.ceiling: £1,500/mo x 11 funds = £198k, against established commodity research houses.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,500/mo x 11 funds = £198k less ~£15k costs = £183k. Eleven subscribers is reachable but Benchmark Mineral Intelligence and similar own this space. Realistic: 4-5 = £72-90k.
carries: Powerful policy tailwind and a China-processing angle incumbents cover less well.
kills: Specialist incumbents with deep mining expertise she cannot match quickly.
test: Ask three commodity PMs what they read on critical minerals and what it misses.
test_pass: They name a China processing blind spot.
test_fail: They are well served by existing specialists.
